note: Each IRW item is a framing PAIR, not a single administered question, and `resp` is a DERIVED score: the study's Codebook.xlsx variables sheet defines every column as "The absolute difference between loss and gain frame on the ' pesticide ' item" (and likewise for the other 13), so resp 0-5 is |rating of frame A - rating of frame B|, not a rating. Consequences for this file: (a) item_text carries BOTH administered wordings, prefixed 'Gain frame:'/'Loss frame:' for the RC_ items and 'Positive frame:'/'Negative frame:' for the AF_ items -- those four labels are the study's own terms (Codebook.xlsx) but the bracketing is IRW scaffolding, not text anyone read; (b) option_text is blank for all 84 rows, because a derived difference score has no administered anchors -- the 1-6 anchors that DO exist ('Definitely would choose A' etc.) label the raw frame ratings, which are not what this table stores, so shipping them would mislabel resp. MAPPING CHAIN, all from the study's own files (OSF j5n6f, CC BY 4.0): the IRW item code IS the Data_Full.csv column name verbatim (data/Resistance.R only pivots, it renames nothing); Codebook.xlsx names each column's referent ('pesticide', 'condom', 'soldiers', ...); and the Qualtrics survey definition JRP_Study_NAmerica_fin.qsf ties each DataExportTag (RCG1..7, RCL1..7, AFP1..7, AFN1..7) to its administered QuestionText. item_text is transcribed from the .qsf, i.e. from the survey as fielded, cross-read against RtF_Materials_En.pdf. TWO DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS FROM THE .qsf, both disclosed: (1) RCG4/RCL2 contain the piped field ${e://Field/Country}; it is replaced by the study's own published rendering of it, 'Canada/the United States' (RtF_Materials_En.pdf, RC gain Problem 4). (2) RCL3's .qsf text reads 'there is a 33% chance that the nothing will be lost' -- a typo in the fielded survey; it is shipped as fielded, not silently corrected to the materials PDF's 'that nothing will be lost'. instructions is blank by design: the RC and AF blocks were given DIFFERENT instructions, so both sit in section_prompt per section (Resistance_RC, Resistance_AF) and nothing is whole-table. LANGUAGE: the table pools two samples administered in two languages -- 261 North American respondents read the English shipped here, 245 Bulgarian respondents read a validated Bulgarian translation (OSF Materials_BG/RtF_Materials_Bg.pdf). The schema holds one administered wording per item, so the English is shipped, language and the _translated columns are omitted, and the Bulgarian half is disclosed in public_note. This is NOT text_source=translated_substitute: the shipped English is an administered version, not a stand-in for one. RIGHTS: no restriction locatable to quote, so silence-is-permission applies. The wording came from the Geiger/Vintr/Rachev OSF deposit, which is CC BY 4.0 (osf.io/j5n6f, license 'CC-By Attribution 4.0 International' via the OSF API). The originating instrument is the Resistance to Framing scale of the A-DMC (Bruine de Bruin, Parker & Fischhoff 2007); SJDM's DMIDI page for it (sjdm.org/dmidi/Adult_-_Decision_Making_Competence.html), which distributes the measure itself as PDF/HTML plus a scoring key, states no fee, no non-commercial clause, no permission requirement and no redistribution bar -- checked 2026-09-10. No row exists for this instrument in instrument_rights_register.csv and none was written (a round may not write a ship-shaped row).
public_note: `resp` in this table is not a rating: it is the absolute difference (0-5) between the respondent's ratings of the two frames of each framing problem, so each row's `item_text` carries both administered wordings and `option_text` is deliberately blank -- and the shipped wording is the English version, which only the 261 North American respondents read, the other 245 having answered a validated Bulgarian translation.
